title: Haynesville Shale Mineral Rights
metaTitle: Haynesville Shale Mineral Rights: Gas-Price Whiplash
metaDescription: Haynesville minerals in Caddo, Bossier, DeSoto, or Panola county live and die on gas prices. Here's how that volatility should shape your sale decision.
heroLead: No basin in this country swings its drilling pace with gas prices the way the Haynesville does. Understanding that rhythm matters more here than almost any other single fact.
intro: The Haynesville sits under northwest Louisiana and the adjoining corner of East Texas — Caddo, Bossier, DeSoto, and Red River parishes on the Louisiana side, Panola, Harrison, and Shelby counties on the Texas side. It's a pure dry gas play, which means unlike an oil basin where royalty checks stay relatively steady, Haynesville income tracks the Henry Hub gas price almost directly, and operators here throttle drilling up and down with that price faster than in almost any oil-weighted basin.

sections.heading: The operators and what drives their pace
paragraphs: Chesapeake, now operating as Expand Energy after its merger with Southwestern, remains one of the largest Haynesville producers alongside Comstock Resources, Aethon Energy, and a meaningful presence from Southwestern's legacy assets. These companies idled significant drilling during the 2023-2024 gas price collapse and have been bringing rigs back as LNG export demand from Gulf Coast terminals has firmed up pricing. That LNG demand story is arguably the single biggest driver of Haynesville activity right now — proximity to export infrastructure gives this basin's gas a demand outlet that landlocked dry gas plays don't have.

sections.heading: Why your royalty check moves so much
paragraphs: If you've owned Haynesville minerals for several years, you've likely watched your check swing by half or more between good gas-price months and weak ones, without any change in the well's actual production volume. That's the nature of a dry gas royalty — you're getting paid a percentage of revenue, and gas revenue is entirely a function of price times volume, with no oil cushion to smooth things out.

This volatility matters directly for a sale decision. A buyer pricing your interest during a gas price trough will offer less than the same buyer would during a strong LNG-demand quarter, so timing a sale against the gas price cycle, to the extent you can, is worth thinking about rather than assuming your interest is worth a fixed number regardless of when you sell.

sections.heading: Core versus edge in this basin
paragraphs: Caddo and DeSoto parishes in Louisiana, along with the adjoining Texas counties near the state line, sit in the thickest, most productive core of the play and have held operator commitment even through the 2023 downturn. Move toward the northern or western edges of the mapped Haynesville extent and well results get more inconsistent, which is where buyer interest thins out fastest during any price weakness.

sections.heading: Listing during a recovering gas market
paragraphs: With LNG demand pulling Haynesville activity back up after a rough stretch, this is a basin where a competitive listing process can capture real upside if buyers are actively repositioning for renewed drilling. A direct offer locked in during the recent downturn may not reflect where buyer appetite has moved since, so it's worth getting a current read on the market rather than assuming an old quote still applies.

sections.heading: Louisiana versus Texas side differences
paragraphs: While the Haynesville is a single formation, the Louisiana parishes and Texas counties that make it up operate under different state regulatory frameworks, different severance tax structures, and in some cases different typical lease terms that have developed over the play's history. Louisiana's parish-based system and Texas's county-based system also mean title research and courthouse records are organized differently depending on which side of the state line your minerals sit, which is a practical detail worth confirming with anyone helping you evaluate an offer, since it affects how quickly ownership and production history can be verified. Louisiana's civil-law property framework also handles some mineral ownership and succession questions differently than Texas's common-law approach, which matters for heirs sorting out inherited interests across the state line. If your family's Haynesville minerals passed through several generations without a clean succession or probate record, that gap can complicate a sale regardless of which side of the state line you're on, and resolving it before listing tends to go faster than trying to fix it mid-negotiation.

faqs.question: Why did my Haynesville royalty check drop so much over the past couple years?
faqs.answer: Dry gas royalties track Henry Hub pricing directly, and gas prices fell sharply in 2023-2024, which reduced revenue even where production volumes held steady.

faqs.question: Is Haynesville drilling activity picking back up?
faqs.answer: Operators have been adding rigs back as LNG export demand from Gulf Coast terminals has supported gas prices, though the pace still depends on where prices sit.

faqs.question: Does LNG export demand actually affect my mineral value?
faqs.answer: Yes, indirectly. Stronger gas demand supports higher prices and more drilling, both of which improve what buyers are willing to pay for producing or undeveloped Haynesville minerals.

faqs.question: Should I wait for gas prices to rise before selling?
faqs.answer: That depends on your risk tolerance and cash needs; a broker can walk through recent pricing trends and current buyer appetite so you're deciding with current information rather than guessing.
